\section{Technical Analysis}
\label{sec:tech}
Infrared reflectography reveals an underdrawing in a dry
medium, with hatching that follows the workshop's habitual
left-to-right strokes.
The pigment layer contains the expensive ultramarine that,
in the dated works discussed in Section~\ref{introduction},
is reserved for the mantle of the Virgin.
Dendrochronology gives a felling date after 1482, consistent
with the chapel inventory rather than with the early
nineteenth-century copy that earlier catalogues proposed.
The craquelure pattern, finally, matches that of the two
signed workshop pieces in the Berlin gallery.
